analysis.one_liner: Coal India is the world's largest coal mining company, a Government of India-controlled near-monopoly that mines and sells coal mostly to power plants under long-term Fuel Supply Agreements (FSA) plus open e-auctions.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (declared ~29 Oct 2026) showed consolidated net profit of roughly ₹6,500-6,550 crore (sources vary between ₹6,516 cr/+53% YoY and ₹6,547 cr/+57% YoY) and revenue up 21% YoY to ₹44,179 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding to ~19.2%. The board declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25/share, but the stock still fell ~3% post-results as analysts flagged flat e-auction realisations; the exact record date for this payout isn't in the verified dividend history yet (last confirmed payout: ₹5.25 on 2026-09-04).
analysis.plain_terms: Coal India looks statistically cheap - a single-digit P/E and a near-7% dividend yield - which sounds like a bargain, but the business is a government-controlled near-monopoly where most of its coal is sold at FSA-contracted prices it doesn't fully control, and labour costs reset periodically through national wage agreements. The 53-57% profit jump this quarter is partly a bounce-back: last year's Q2 (Q2 FY26) profit had fallen 32% YoY on monsoon disruption and wage-related costs, so this quarter is recovering toward, not necessarily beating, the level from two years ago. The real question is whether the current e-auction price recovery is durable or another short-term swing.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY26 (year-ago quarter) saw profit fall ~32% YoY to about ₹4,260 crore, blamed by management and the Coal Minister on heavy monsoon-related mining disruption and wage-related cost pressure. Q2 FY27 profit of ~₹6,500-6,550 crore is therefore a recovery off a depressed base - back near the ~₹6,265 crore level implied for Q2 FY25, rather than a fresh high. Sales volume rose 13% YoY (FSA volumes +12%, e-auction volumes +51% off a smaller base) and overall realisation improved 7% to ₹2,346/tonne, but e-auction prices were largely flat YoY during the quarter itself; management flagged that the benefit of higher e-auction prices from August 2026 should show up more in Q3 FY27. A wage hike for non-executive staff effective July 2026 is an ongoing cost headwind. Separately, October 2026 output (67.2 MT) and offtake (70.3 MT, a record) were up ~19% YoY, but cumulative April-October FY27 production growth is just 0.7%, meaning the full-year production ramp still has a long way to go.
analysis.performance_read: No splits or demergers are on record for Coal India (has_corporate_action: false), so the price trail doesn't need any corporate-action adjustment. On the numbers given, the stock has beaten both the Nifty and peer NMDC over 1, 3 and 5 years (5Y: +245.7% vs Nifty +28.6% and NMDC +146.5%). It is currently ₹389, down 17.1% from a June 2026 peak of ₹469.36 - a genuine price drawdown, not a crash caused by any spin-off or restructuring.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades around 7-8x trailing earnings versus a mining-sector median closer to 13x, with ROE near 28% and ROCE near 35% - both above sector medians. It is cheap partly for structural reasons (government ownership discount, price caps on FSA volumes, periodic wage-cost shocks, ESG/coal-transition overhang) rather than purely because the market is mispricing it. Whether that discount is excessive depends on how durable the e-auction price recovery and volume growth turn out to be - not something this report can settle.
analysis.growth_read: This quarter's growth was largely volume-led (sales volume +13% YoY, e-auction volume +51% off a low base) with margin also expanding (EBITDA margin up ~120bps to 19.2%), so it's a mix rather than margin-only. However, the headline YoY comparisons benefit from a weak year-ago base, and full fiscal-year production growth (April-October: +0.7%) is far more muted than the single strong month of October (+19.3%) suggests - the year-to-date picture is weaker than the quarterly headline implies.
analysis.health_read: Company-level cash flow generation from mining operations is historically strong, but the cash/debt figures pulled from different sources this time were internally inconsistent (one source implied an implausibly large net-cash position relative to its own stated cash and debt numbers) - not verified, check on Screener for current net debt/cash figures. The more relevant risk for Coal India is business/regulatory risk (wage-negotiation cycles, FSA pricing, environmental and production constraints) rather than balance-sheet leverage risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The President of India (Government of India) holds about 61.13% as promoter, so pledging - a concern for leveraged private promoters - doesn't meaningfully apply here. Domestic institutions (DIIs, including likely LIC and mutual funds) hold roughly 23%, while foreign institutional holding is small and reportedly declining. No specific marquee non-government investor stands out on the register worth flagging by name.
strengths: Revenue grew 21% YoY to ₹44,179 crore in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA margin expanding ~120bps to about 19.2%
TTM dividend yield of 6.81% (₹26.5/share), among the highest for a large-cap PSU
5-year stock return of 245.72% comfortably ahead of the Nifty (28.58%) and peer NMDC (146.46%)
ROE (~28%) and ROCE (~35%) running well above the sector's quoted median P/E-implied profitability benchmarks
watchpoints: Cumulative production for April-October FY27 is up only 0.7% YoY despite October alone rising 19.3% - the year's production targets are still largely unmet
Q2 FY27's 53-57% profit jump is measured against a Q2 FY26 base that itself had fallen 32% YoY on monsoon disruption and wage costs - genuine multi-year growth looks far more modest
A non-executive wage hike effective July 2026 is an active cost headwind, and Coal India's wage-negotiation cycles have caused sharp profit swings before
E-auction realisations were flat YoY in the reported quarter, which is why the stock fell ~3% even after the profit beat; stock is also 17.1% below its June 2026 peak
analysis.one_thing: Whether the e-auction price pickup management flagged from August 2026 actually shows up in Q3 FY27 numbers - that distinguishes a genuine margin/pricing recovery from another base-effect-driven headline.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue growth (+21% to ₹44,179 crore) and the Q2 FY26 base-year decline (-32% to ~₹4,262 crore) were corroborated across multiple independent sources. The exact Q2 FY27 net profit figure varies between ₹6,516 crore (+53%) and ₹6,547 crore (+57%) depending on the source - both are reported, neither confirmed as definitive. Balance sheet cash/debt figures from aggregator sites were internally inconsistent and are not verified - check Coal India's latest filing or Screener directly for current net debt/cash position. Promoter pledge status (none) and shareholding percentages are as reported by data aggregators, not the company's own filing.
